{'id': '0', 'contents': 'This year has officially become the year of the super app. OpenAI recently launched its own super app but promptly admitted that “it’s a bit of a mess.” Now the CEO of Microsoft has also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.'}

{'id': '1', 'contents': 'Microsoft Copilot “Super App” to Integrate Cowork, Chat, Coding and More'}

{'id': '2', 'contents': 'Microsoft is developing an AI “super app” that brings together Copilot’s chat, coding and agent capabilities. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday’s earnings call that the app will launch this year and span “consumer and commercial experiences.” “Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork to Autopilot,” Nadella said. “This quarter we will bring these Copilot experiences — including coding — together into a single super app… This is an important step and I look forward to sharing more details shortly.”'}

{'id': '3', 'contents': 'OpenAI’s launch of its own “super app” has already turned into a debacle, but that clearly hasn’t deterred other companies from following the super app playbook.'}

{'id': '4', 'contents': 'Perhaps Microsoft can deliver a one-stop app with fewer stumbles than OpenAI.'}

{'id': '5', 'contents': 'That said, CEO Satya Nadella has also recently suggested the company is shifting from apps to an agent-centric approach. The AI era is still new, and the trends and best practices for building AI interfaces are still in flux.'}

{'id': '6', 'contents': 'As for Apple, there are no signs it is moving toward a super app approach, and it continues to roll out separate, specialised new apps. Whether that strategy changes in the future will be worth watching.'}

{'id': '7', 'contents': 'What do you think of the recent “super app” craze? Share your thoughts in the comments.'}
